memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will remember my covenant between me and you and all living creatures of every kind. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life." - Gen 9:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives us a beautiful glimpse into how He relates to His own promise. When the clouds gather and the rainbow appears, God says, "I will remember my covenant." The very moment when storm clouds might stir up fear is the moment God points to His promise of mercy. Where we might see threatening skies, God has placed a reminder of His faithful love.

Think about the timing. The rainbow does not appear on clear, sunny days. It appears when clouds have gathered and rain is falling - in the shadow of what once meant judgement. And precisely there, in the clouds, God shows His covenant of mercy. His grace shines brightest against the backdrop of the storm.

This is how God so often works in our lives. It is in our cloudy days, our seasons of fear and difficulty, that He most clearly shows us His faithfulness. When the skies darken, He does not want us to see only the storm; He wants us to see His promise arching over it. The clouds are real, but so is the covenant.

Whatever storm clouds hang over your life today, God invites you to look for the rainbow - to remember that His mercy triumphs and His promises hold. He has bound Himself to His people in an unbreakable covenant, sealed forever in Christ. When the clouds gather, remember: God remembers His promise, and His mercy is greater than any storm.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- In your cloudy seasons, do you look for the storm or for God's promise?
- How does it comfort you that God shows His mercy in the midst of the clouds?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that in my cloudy days You point me to Your promise. When storms gather and fear rises, help me look for the rainbow of Your mercy, and rest in Your unbreakable covenant love.
